title: Add first-class adventure module support
description:
Problem

Eshyra currently has campaign state persistence and static rules-pack content, but it does not have a first-class representation for pre-written adventure or dungeon module content. That leaves no clear place for starter adventure content to go and forces setting-scale material such as the Emberfall setting to carry responsibilities that belong to a scenario-scale module.

A campaign template should represent a broad reusable world or setting, in the same general scope category as The Grand Duchy of Karameikos, Dragonlance, or Forgotten Realms. A dungeon or adventure module should represent an authored playable scenario, in the same general scope category as Castle Amber or The Lost Mine of Phandelver.

Goal

Introduce adventure modules as first-class immutable authored content, distinct from rules packs, campaign templates, and mutable campaign instance state. A campaign instance should be able to bind to one or more active modules via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, expose bounded module context to the DM runtime, persist module progress, and record player-driven deviations without mutating the source module.
design:
Architectural rule - four layers, defined in ADR 0012 (eshyra-eh54.1):

1. Rules packs define mechanical truth (immutable authored/imported source).
2. Campaign templates define reusable worlds/settings (immutable setting-scale source).
3. Adventure modules define authored playable scenarios (immutable scenario-scale source).
4. Campaign instances define actual play history and mutable state.

Adventure modules are immutable authored scenario content. A campaign may contain one or more campaign-owned adventure runs or module bindings that reference modules and record module-specific progress. These adventure runs are part of campaign instance state, not a fifth content/state layer. Do not introduce an "adventure instance" as a peer top-level layer.

Runtime adaptation belongs in campaign instance state as discovered facts, altered facts, completed objectives, revealed secrets, encounter outcomes, and explicit deviations from module assumptions - never written back to the module source.

This epic should avoid third-party adventure conversion until the module schema and runtime destination exist. The frozen starter-content bead can remain blocked until this epic creates somewhere for that content to go.

Naming glossary (see ADR 0012 and eshyra-eh54.7):
- Emberfall - the setting-scale village/region; campaign-template concept.
- The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - the first-party starter adventure module title (scenario-scale).
- Ember Hollow - informal project shorthand only; not a separate canonical entity.
- EMBERFALL_HOLLOW - the existing legacy sample that conflates setting and scenario, to be split by later eh54 work.
acceptance_criteria:
- Eshyra has a documented architecture distinction between the four layers: rules packs, campaign templates/settings, adventure modules, and campaign instances (ADR 0012).
- Adventure module content is represented as immutable authored source material.
- Module progress is represented as mutable campaign instance state via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, not as a fifth peer layer.
- A campaign instance can bind to one or more active adventure modules without mutating module source.
- The DM runtime has a path to receive bounded module context without dumping an entire module each turn.
- The Emberfall setting is preserved as setting-scale campaign template content, not forced to become the starter module itself.
- Follow-up work exists for a small first-party starter module (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall) that serves as the gameplay hello-world scenario.
